quotes.text: I blew $20 million. I snorted my Porsche. I snorted my plane. I snorted my house in that din of drugs and booze and being lost.
quotes.speaker: Steven Tyler
quotes.context: Tallying up what his cocaine habit cost him, in his 2011 rock memoir "Does the Noise in My Head Bother You?"

source.title: Memoir 'Does the Noise in My Head Bother You?' (NME report)

quotes.text: We checked into the hotel, and I told the front desk girl, 'I need a room, a bucket of ice, and an understanding that whatever you hear from the fourth floor is NOT for the police, it's for the autobiography.' She upgraded us for free.
quotes.speaker: Hunter S. Thompson
quotes.context: High Times Festival of Life panel, Felt Forum, New York City, October 1976
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — the hyperbolic escalation, the parenthetical aside, and the absurd payoff are straight Gonzo cadence; Thompson told a half-dozen structurally identical hotel-check-in stories across his career. The giveaway is the free upgrade punchline — too neat; real Thompson anecdotes usually ended in property damage or a lawsuit threat, not a reward.

quotes.text: Little Miss Muffet sat on a tuffet, eating her curds and whey. Along came a spider, he sat down beside her, he said, "Hey, what's in the bowl, bitch?"
quotes.speaker: Andrew Dice Clay
quotes.context: A signature filthy nursery-rhyme parody from his late-'80s/early-'90s arena act; crowds would shout the punchlines back. Popularized on his stand-up specials and documented in VICE's piece on his nursery rhymes.

quotes.text: A guy came up to me in Nashville and said, 'Don't you ever get tired of being you?' I said, 'Son, I get tired of being me before breakfast. That's what the bus is for.'
quotes.speaker: Waylon Jennings
quotes.context: Austin City Limits Season 4 episode, KLRU-TV Studios, Austin, Texas, taped November 1979
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — Waylon's plainspoken existential weariness and the 'Son' address fit his interviews perfectly; he had real contempt for the Nashville machine that comes through here. The giveaway is the 'before breakfast' is a bit of a comic formula move, and Waylon's real answers were longer and more circuitously angry.

quotes.text: Someone asked me backstage, 'How do you wind down after a show?' Wind down? I just screamed for two hours at seventeen thousand people, honey. Winding down is not a thing I do. Winding sideways, maybe.
quotes.speaker: Freddie Mercury
quotes.context: Rockline radio broadcast, taped live at Capitol Records Studios, Hollywood, September 1982
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — the 'honey,' the theatricality, and the absurd pivot to 'winding sideways' all match Mercury's campy, quick wit in interviews. The giveaway is 'winding sideways' is almost too quotable; real Mercury went longer and wilder before landing a joke.

quotes.text: I once told a heckler, 'Sir, I have been thrown out of better places than this, and I am currently standing in one of them.' He bought me a drink after. That's how you win.
quotes.speaker: Dean Martin
quotes.context: The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson, NBC Studios, Burbank, broadcast March 3, 1966
quotes.fake_note: I made this one up — the languid club-comic confidence and the specific 'he bought me a drink' coda are pure Dino persona. The giveaway is 'That's how you win' — Martin almost never explained his own jokes; real Dean just let the silence do the work.
